Crab Breeze / cockpit review / Breeze chassis

The Breeze cockpit, from the pilot's seat

Work in progress, 2026-10-24: sealed, with an all-view screen wall in place of the glass (your direction). The boarding sequence (the mech sits down, hatches and flaps open, steam and mist) comes next on this page. Quick bake: 1024 px, 16 samples.

This is the view you fight from. Drag to turn your head, scroll to zoom. The cockpit is sealed: the walls above the consoles are one wall of screens (Gundam's all-view monitor) showing what the mech's cameras see, with the HUD drawn on it. Every panel is modelled in Blender and baked to texture the Star Crew way (plates, screws, backlit buttons, guarded switches, dials, stencilled warnings, live circuit boards behind inspection windows), then the cabin's light and occlusion are baked over it: sky through the canopy, the glare shield and sill floodlights, the dome lamp, a red footwell lamp and the glow of the screens.

What you are looking at

  • Dash: three MFDs (damage and heat, the tactical radar, weapons and jet fuel) in bezels with real push buttons; the caution and warning panel and master lights on the left; reactor and jet fuel standby gauges on the right; the mode row (walk, skate, jet).
  • All-view screen: the sealed shell is lined with screen tiles showing the outside; Screens on/off plays the tile by tile power-up. The HUD (pitch ladder, heading, speed, height, missile lock, Ace Combat style) is drawn on the screen ahead.
  • Left console: the throttle in its quadrant (idle, walk, run, skate, and the jet gate), reactor pumps, comms keypad.
  • Right console: the twist grip that turns the torso, the guarded master arm, weapon select, countermeasures.
  • Knees: standby gauges and the emergency panel in hazard stripes: reactor scram, jet cutoff, jettison arms, under red and yellow guards. The eject handle sits between your knees.
  • Walls and bulkhead: live circuit boards behind inspection windows with their 880 V warnings, the main breaker board, the reactor coolant lines, the canopy jettison handle.

What it costs

Measured off the glb and the bake. A cloud session has no GPU, so frame time is not measured here (CLAUDE.md 7).

What is placeholder

  • The screens and HUD show pictures of what they will show; in the game each number is the simulation's own (CLAUDE.md 6.1), drawn live on the SCREEN_* and HUD_combiner nodes.
  • The light was baked for the earlier glass canopy (sky through it); the next bake lights the sealed cabin from the screen wall and the cabin lamps.
  • The world on the screens is a stand-in city captured from the eye.
  • No pilot body or hands yet, and the world outside is a stand-in.

The panels, as modelled

Each panel rendered under a fixed key light at one scale. The cockpit uses its albedo, normal, occlusion and emission maps, not this picture.
